proposed_changes.delta: Only peer source; initialize write_closed false, fail new RequestReceived or per-connection commands once true, drain/discard closed-side control output in flush, mark true immediately after successful actual base SHUT_WR.
proposed_changes.adoption_guard: Require baseline SHA match and each old fragment exactly once; abort on mismatch. Output hash is exact unformatted replacement result.

write_side_contract.state: write_closed is independent of eof. It becomes true only after successful socket.socket.shutdown(client['socket'], socket.SHUT_WR), before ACK, while self.lock remains held. Shutdown exceptions propagate without marking successful state.
write_side_contract.locking: Existing serve receive_data/flush and command paths already hold the same RLock. Request guard, flush guard, successful SHUT_WR and flag publication are serialized; no new lock or process.
write_side_contract.queued_controls: Once write_closed is true, flush calls public conn.data_to_send() solely to drain the in-memory output buffer, then returns before body processing/sendall. These bytes cannot be transmitted after SHUT_WR; retaining the buffer provides no protocol value and may accumulate until real remote close. No control success/physical event is fabricated.
write_side_contract.application_safety: The sole completed /health/no pending command precondition remains unchanged. New RequestReceived after half-close fails before automatic response creation; subsequent per-connection JSON commands fail before mutating/sending. stop remains the existing global stop path. Thus discarded output is limited to receive-side control output from an already completed stream; unexpected events/protocol errors retain existing failure handling.
write_side_contract.error_safety: No exception catch, retry, BrokenPipe suppression or error-to-EOF mapping is added. Every send/flush/shutdown error before successful half-close and all unrelated errors retain existing failure paths. Invalid writes after half-close become explicit fixture errors instead of being silently discarded.
write_side_contract.read_side: No changes to sock.recv, SSL decoding, eof flag, exception classes, physical events, original finally sock.close, stop forced accounting, worker joins or listener lifecycle. No private SSL/client state written.
